newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vertigo keeps German shares off records at start.
newsitem.headline: Vertigo keeps German shares off records at start.

text.p: Overnight records on Wall Street sent German shares within a hair's breadth of new records early on Tuesday, but the surge lost its momentum amid nerves at the market's dizzying levels and a slip by Bunds.
"It's just not easy to believe in highs like this," said a Frankfurt DAX futures trader.
"A lot of the rise seems to be just covering short positions."
The IBIS DAX index seesawed through the early session to hit a high of 3,611.10 points, just off its record of 3,612.46, before easing back to trade down 4.97 points at 3,588.17.
June DTB DAX futures were up 2.5 points at 3,596 points, having earlier shown gains of 25 points.
Some dealers remained confident that the market could regain momentum, especially during the DAX floor trading session when more liquidity comes into the market.
"There is a positive feeling about," said another trader. "We should see more records."

One of the pressures on early trade was a slide by Deutsche Telekom AG, partly correcting a recent surge, after the telecommunications giant released 1996 data which confirmed bullish forecasts, but did not surprise, dealers said.
The company posted group net profit of 1.8 billion marks for the year in a report released ahead of its annual news conference later today.
Telekom, which notched up gains of as much as five percent at its height on Monday, was down 88 pfennigs, or two percent, at 40.25 marks an hour into electronic dealings.
Also trading heavily was Deutsche Bank AG, which set an early record of 97.75 marks before easing to trade down 25 pfennigs at 96.60 marks.
Schering AG also lost on profit taking after releasing first quarter data.
Chemical firm Henkel KGaA also fell, dropping 1.80 marks to 92.50, after reporting a seven percent rise in pre-tax profit for the first quarter. Dealers also attributed this decline to profit taking.
